name: Mauritius
description: Mauritius offers expats political stability, a dynamic economy, and an appealing tax regime within a stunning tropical setting. It draws remote workers, retirees, investors, and families seeking a high quality of life and a welcoming multicultural environment.
longdescription: Mauritius, an island nation in the Indian Ocean, has become a top destination for expatriates due to its blend of natural beauty, stable governance, and economic dynamism. The multicultural society, where English, French, and Mauritian Creole are widely spoken, facilitates easy integration for newcomers. The economy is robust, driven significantly by tourism and a well-developed financial services sector, creating opportunities for professionals and investors. Expats can expect a relaxed island lifestyle complemented by modern infrastructure, including good private healthcare facilities and international schools. While the cost of living can be higher than expected for imported goods and luxury services, local produce and a mindful lifestyle can make it affordable. The government actively promotes foreign investment and offers various residency pathways, though recent changes in tax and residency requirements emphasize a longer-term commitment to the island.

visas.name: Mauritius Premium Visa
visas.description: Mauritius's digital nomad and long-stay visa allows remote workers, retirees, and tourists to live in Mauritius for up to a year, with income sourced from outside the island.
benefits: Live and work remotely from a tropical island
Tax-exempt status for foreign income during the first 6 months
visas.path_to_residency_description: Does not count toward permanent residency.

visas.name: Mauritius Retired Residence Permit
visas.description: A 10-year residence permit for non-citizens aged 50+ who can commit to transferring a minimum of $1,500 monthly (or $18,000 annually) into a Mauritian bank account.
benefits: 10-year residency in a safe, tropical nation
Permit holders can invest in local businesses
No tax on capital gains or inheritance
visas.path_to_residency_description: Eligible to apply for a 20-year Permanent Residence Permit after 3 consecutive years.

visas.name: Mauritius Investor Occupation Permit
visas.description: An occupation permit combining work and residence for investors establishing an business in Mauritius with an initial investment of at least $50,000.
benefits: Live, work, and do business in Mauritius
Exempt from custom duties on office equipment
visas.path_to_residency_description: Eligible to apply for a 20-year Permanent Residence Permit after 3 consecutive years with minimum annual turnover.

Citizenship by Descent.desc: Citizenship is automatically granted to individuals with a Mauritian parent. This applies to persons born in Mauritius or those born outside Mauritius to Mauritian-born citizens, under Sections 20(3) and 23 of the Constitution. Registration with Mauritian civil or diplomatic authorities may be required to confirm nationality.

Naturalization.desc: The general path to naturalization requires a person to have held permanent residency in Mauritius for at least 7 years, having lived there for 5 of those years, with no absence from the country in the last 12 months of that 5-year period. For investors, naturalization is possible after a minimum investment of USD 500,000 and continuous residence in Mauritius for at least 2 years immediately prior to applying. Applicants must demonstrate good character, financial stability, and integration into Mauritian society. Naturalized citizens may be required to renounce their existing citizenship unless special permission is granted.

Birthright.desc: Citizenship by birth is available for persons born before October 1, 1995, from foreign parents who were residents of Mauritius, or directly from Mauritian citizens. For persons born after October 1, 1995, citizenship is conferred if at least one parent is a Mauritian citizen. Birth in Mauritius alone does not automatically grant citizenship to children of foreign parents unless specific statutory requirements are met.

Spouse and Family.desc: A foreign spouse of a Mauritian citizen can apply for citizenship after 4 years of marriage and continuous cohabitation in Mauritius. Minor children (under 18) can be registered as Mauritian citizens after a parent becomes naturalized, without needing to fulfill separate residency requirements. Other dependents, such as elderly parents or adult dependents, do not have a direct citizenship pathway through the applicant's status and would typically need to meet standard naturalization requirements.

tax_advice:
*   **Tax Year:** The fiscal year in Mauritius runs from July 1 to June 30 of the following year.
*   **Tax Residency:** An individual is considered a tax resident if they reside in Mauritius for at least 183 days during the fiscal year, or for at least 270 days when combining the time spent in the current and two preceding fiscal years. Tax residents are liable to tax on their worldwide income, while non-residents are taxed only on Mauritian-sourced income.
*   **Personal Income Tax:** Mauritius employs a progressive tax system. Income up to Rs 500,000 is taxed at 0%. Income between Rs 500,001 and Rs 1,000,000 is taxed at 10%. Any chargeable income exceeding Rs 1,000,000 is taxed at 20%. A new 35% tax rate applies to chargeable income above MUR 12 million, effective from the income year ending June 30, 2027, replacing the Fair Share Contribution.
*   **Tax Deductions:** Individuals are eligible for deductions for dependents. Foreign-sourced income not remitted to Mauritius may be exempt from local taxation.
*   **Corporate Income Tax:** A flat corporate tax rate of 15% is applied. Companies may benefit from an 80% exemption on certain income categories, such as interest income and foreign dividends, subject to substance requirements, which can reduce the effective tax rate to as low as 3%. The Fair Share Contribution of 5% applies to corporations with annual chargeable income exceeding Rs 24 million for the years of assessment 2026/2027, 2027/2028, and 2028/2029.
*   **VAT:** The standard Value Added Tax (VAT) rate is 15%. Services provided by Management companies are now VAT exempt. Foreign suppliers are no longer required to register for VAT if the customer is VAT registered.
*   **Other Taxes:** Mauritius levies no wealth tax, capital gains tax, or direct inheritance tax.
*   **Double Taxation Agreements:** Mauritius has signed 43 double taxation agreements, which can help mitigate double taxation for income earned overseas.
local_tips:
*   **Cost of Living:** While generally lower than Western Europe, Mauritius can be expensive for specific items. A single person's estimated monthly costs, excluding rent, can range from $590.9 to $2,500, and a family of four from $1,800 to $5,500. Expect high costs for imported goods, cars, private healthcare, and international schooling. Rent for a 1-bedroom apartment in expat hubs like Grand Baie ranges from $330-$775 per month, while luxury villas are significantly higher.
*   **Language:** English and French are the official languages, widely used in government and business. Mauritian Creole is the most commonly spoken language in daily life, and learning some phrases can enhance integration.
*   **Safety:** Mauritius is considered a politically stable and safe country with a relatively low crime rate. However, expats should be aware of petty theft, particularly in tourist areas.
*   **Registration/Residency:** Several pathways exist:
    *   **Premium Visa:** Ideal for remote workers, retirees, and business owners, offering a stay of up to one year, renewable. Requires proof of sufficient funds (e.g., $1,500 monthly income), health insurance, and a clean criminal record. No local employment is permitted.
    *   **Occupation Permit (OP):** A combined work and residence permit valid for up to 10 years. Categories include Professionals (requiring a minimum monthly salary of MUR 60,000, or MUR 30,000 for ProPass and MUR 250,000 for Expert Pass), Investors (minimum USD 50,000 investment in a Mauritian business), and Self-Employed individuals (USD 50,000 investment with income targets).
    *   **Residence Permit by Property Investment:** Obtainable by investing a minimum of USD 375,000 in approved real estate schemes (PDS, Smart City, IRS, RES, G+2). This grants a 20-year or lifetime residence permit for the investor and their dependents. Note that from July 1, 2026, the registration duty for non-citizens purchasing property in approved schemes will increase from 5% to 10%.
    *   **Retired Non-Citizen Permit:** For individuals aged 50 and above, requiring a minimum monthly transfer of USD 2,000 (USD 24,000 annually) into a local bank account. This permit is initially valid for 5 years and renewable, potentially leading to a 20-year permanent residence after five consecutive years and cumulative transfers of USD 200,000.
    *   **Permanent Residence Permit (PRP):** The eligibility period to apply for PRP has been extended from 3 years to 5 years for most categories, including Investors, Professionals, and the Self-Employed.
